# OpenAI DevDay 2026 - 20 launches and a new assistant
## Dots - OpenAI joins the AI assistant race ( [X](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2104984504133918973), [Blog](https://openai.com/index/introducing-dots/))
It works 24/7, you can talk to it in Slack or Teams, and there’s an interface that looks like a phone call.

# Meta launches Muse, a free 24/7 agent with its own computer - the OpenClaw for your mom (and you!) ( [X](https://x.com/Muse/status/2097399178376671666), [My thread](https://x.com/altryne/status/2097430715923399135), [Site](https://muse.ai/), [Security](https://security.muse.ai/), [My YT breakdown](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q_PKk3MiR9Y&lc=UgzvucQxbbX3YFOc8HF4AaABAg))
It’s really really fast, and oh... it’s free (up to 100M tokens per week?).

An agent that with your permission can read your emails, browse (and do shopping for you).

## The Zuck shaped elephant in the room : Privacy and Security
Meta is obviously aware of how folks feel and how much sensitive data they allow these agents to accumulate, and on the security page they outline not only the safety measures they took with Muse (noted is the Sentinel additional process that looks at all your conversations and incoming data to your agents and judged independently if it’s safe of if anyone is trying to hack you), Meta is also offering a bounty of up to $300K to anyone that finds a security issue with Muse.
